checked: Act of May 31, 1933, ch. 45, 48 Stat. 108-111, read in full on govinfo: section 2 sum for the Pueblo, section 3 sum for non-Indian claimants, section 6 election, section 10 instalments from fiscal 1937; the quotes in the old breaches were exact.

Act of June 7, 1924, 43 Stat. 636-638, sections 2 and 6, read on govinfo: Board reports cover land granted, confirmed or purchased; section 6 compensation covers land inside granted or confirmed land, for loss through the United States' failure seasonably to prosecute.
Royce 1899 schedule (pp. 920-923, block "Oct. 1, Act of Congress, Stat. L. XI, 374") lists this Pueblo's confirmed grant; matches the file.
Indian Claims Commission, 41 Ind. Cl. Comm. 29 (1977): the "Congress determined the Board was unfair" sentence is a general remark in Santa Clara's case.
Indian Claims Commission, 24 Ind. Cl. Comm. 425 (1971) and 39 Ind. Cl. Comm. 34 (1976), Dockets 354-356 and 358: no Fifth Amendment taking; Congress paid full market value as trustee.
changes: Status lowered from broken to no-breach-found: both breaches (act-of-congress 1924 and government-admission 1933) removed because no opened source ties the divested land to this grant, and the 1933 Act is not an admission that the Board's compensation was inadequate.
The 1933 sums moved to compensation, worded from the Act itself; the ICC 1977 general remark no longer presented as a finding about this Pueblo.
today rewritten to add the 1971 and 1976 Commission rulings (no taking, full market value paid); plain summary removed (not required for no-breach-found and it described the removed breaches).
unverifiable: The Pueblo Lands Board report on this Pueblo (Senate hearings, Survey of Conditions of the Indians, part 20, 1932) could not be opened: HathiTrust full-text search returned a robot challenge, and no other public copy was found.
